timeline.title: NAMC is founded in Oakland, California
timeline.text: Raymond Dones and Joseph Debro start the National Association of Minority Contractors with a handful of members, creating what remains the oldest minority construction trade association in the United States. At the time, federal business with minority firms totaled only about $13 million.

timeline.title: A fast-growing voice
timeline.text: By the mid-1980s membership has grown to roughly 3,500, and federal contracts with minority businesses reached $4.8 billion in fiscal year 1983.

timeline.title: Building Bridges – Crossing Barriers
timeline.text: Membership is open to people of all races and ethnic backgrounds, with a focus on construction industry concerns common to African Americans, Asian Americans, Hispanic Americans, and Native Americans.

timeline.title: Access. Advocacy. Contractor readiness.
timeline.text: NAMC works with corporate partners, strategic allies, and public agencies to connect members to contracts and resources, speak up on legislation, and build capacity through training.

timeline.title: A network built to last
timeline.text: Through local chapters and a growing student chapter program, NAMC counts more than 50 Hall of Fame members and Legacy Builders and an annual project capacity of over a billion dollars nationally.

timeline.title: NAMC Wisconsin Chapter
timeline.text: The Wisconsin Chapter advances education, advocacy, and opportunity for its members from its home in Milwaukee.

timeline.title: National leadership from Wisconsin
timeline.text: Ugo Nwagbaraocha, president of the Wisconsin Chapter and of Diamond Discs International, is elected vice president of the national organization.

timeline.title: The 11th Annual Construction Industry B2B Forum
timeline.text: On November 19, NAMC Wisconsin brings project presentations, utility updates, and strategic matchmaking to the Potawatomi Hotel & Casino Event Center.

timeline.title: The 58th Annual NAMC National Conference
timeline.text: NAMC Wisconsin hosts the national conference in Milwaukee, June 28 to 30, 2027, at the Pfister Hotel, bringing national construction firms, minority contractors, developers, and public agencies together.
